clue.text: Calling for a military take-over

definitions.meaning: a calling is one's trade or profession
an army's seizure and holding of foreign territory

explanation.definitionFit: Both a job and an army's control of conquered land go by this one word.

clue.text: Service boss joins sect of arcane nature

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, the head of a military unit
a cult is a small religious sect

explanation.surface: A senior officer signs up with some mysterious religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult knowledge is hidden and mysterious, the very sense of arcane.

clue.text: Price a pound of rib

parts.note: a price is what something costs
L is the abbreviation for pound (Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone asks the butcher what a pound of rib costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Costal is the anatomical adjective relating to the ribs.

clue.text: Draw attention to particular race-meeting

parts.note: to point to something is to draw attention to it
a point is a particular detail or item

explanation.surface: A racing tipster singles out one specific race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A POINT-TO-POINT is a British amateur steeplechase race meeting across country.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur cross-country horse race, run as a meeting of several such races.

clue.text: Rush to have a meal on the river

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to eat a picnic beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue TEA sits on top of R.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to dash or race at speed.

clue.text: He does everything to break up Ben and Mona

indicators.note: breaking up the couple's names lets their letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to split up a couple called Ben and Mona.
explanation.definitionFit: A street performer playing several instruments alone, and figuratively anyone handling every task single-handed.

clue.text: Foremost character on the staff

parts.note: reads like the leading member of a company's employees, but the staff is the musical stave and the character the symbol written first on it

explanation.definitionFit: This musical sign stands at the very start of each stave, setting the pitch of its lines.

clue.text: 4'2" peg holding the wheel in place

parts.note: four feet two inches is fifty inches, and L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so L INCH
a pin is a small peg

explanation.surface: A carpenter specifies a peg four feet two inches long for a cartwheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 4'2" means fifty inches; written as L (Roman 50) plus INCH it makes the first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A linchpin is the pin through an axle end that keeps a wheel on.

clue.text: At liberty to take wine there off duty?

definitions.text: At liberty to take wine there off duty?

parts.note: being at liberty means being free
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether a harbour lets one buy wine without paying tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a harbour where goods, wine included, can be landed without customs duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour zone where imports escape customs charges.

clue.text: Thespian troupe I confined to base and punished

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a play
gated means confined to college or barracks as a penalty

explanation.surface: A theatre company and the speaker were grounded and disciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke or chastise severely.

clue.text: Never again!

parts.note: an exclamation of regret after a bad experience, read as saying something happened just the one time

explanation.definitionFit: Something done a single time and not repeated is done just that one occasion.

clue.text: Carthusian monastery given licence by the Commons

parts.note: a charter is a formal grant of rights or licence
the House of Commons is called simply the House

explanation.surface: A monastery receives a royal licence through an act of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The English name for a Carthusian religious house, an anglicised form of Chartreuse.

clue.text: Be inclined to get a conservatory

definitions.meaning: to tend towards, or literally to rest against
a glazed room added against a house wall

explanation.definitionFit: A sloping-roofed annexe built against a wall; as a verb phrase, tending towards something.

clue.text: To put a fellow in the tub is a bit of a cheek

parts.note: a bathtub is a bath
a chap is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Climbing into someone else's bathtub is rather impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: A BATH CHAP is a cured pig's cheek, a West Country dish, so 'cheek' is literal rather than impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower half of a pig's jowl, salted and smoked, is a portion of cheek.

clue.text: Highly amused this month by ticklish sensations

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of the current month in old business letters
itches are irritating tingles on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone is laughing because of tickly feelings lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in fits of laughter is an idiom for great amusement.

clue.text: Channel breakwater broken by pilots

parts.note: a sound is a narrow sea channel
a breakwater is a barrier against waves

explanation.surface: A sea wall across the Channel gets smashed by harbour pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilots here are aircraft pilots going supersonic, not harbour pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic aviators break this when they exceed Mach 1.

clue.text: Acknowledged that access was allowed

explanation.definitionFit: Both conceding a point and letting someone enter share one past-tense verb.

clue.text: Has ordered factory-made walking stick

indicators.note: the letters of has are put in a new order

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: Someone buys a mass-produced walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane cut from an ash sapling, used for walking.

clue.text: Querulous assertion that Diana's at peace

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, so Di's
contented means satisfied and at peace

explanation.surface: Someone claims that Diana has found tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the wordplay is the statement that Di is contented.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaining, querulous person is dissatisfied.

clue.text: One small Greek cross on a Mediterranean island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
chi, the Greek letter, is shaped like a cross X

explanation.surface: A single little cross from Greece lies on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An island off Naples in the Tyrrhenian Sea, part of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Zairean leader in Yemen could be a catalyst

indicators.note: the Zairean letter goes inside the shuffled country
Yemen's letters could be arranged another way
a leader is the first letter of the word Zairean

explanation.surface: An African head of state visiting Yemen might spark change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' turns YEMEN into ENYME; 'in' puts Z, from 'Zairean leader', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are biological catalysts speeding up chemical reactions.

clue.text: One young devil initially getting away with it

indicators.note: the imp is placed first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
unity means oneness

explanation.surface: A single little demon first escapes punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is freedom from punishment, the state of escaping consequences.

clue.text: For many are called, but few are "(St Matthew)

definitions.text: For many are called, but few are "(St Matthew)

parts.words: For many are called, but few are "(St Matthew)
parts.note: a Bible verse from St Matthew with its last word missing, to be filled in

explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel line ends with the word for those selected by God.

clue.text: Correct time to repent

parts.note: to rue is to regret or repent

explanation.surface: Now is the right moment to say sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate, right and correct are synonyms.

clue.text: Some returned by carriage

indicators.note: returned means the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some of

explanation.surface: A few people came home by horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn cart.

clue.text: Painstakingly made, though in a crude manner

parts.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though
roughly means crudely

explanation.surface: Something is carefully made, though roughly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefully and completely, attending to every detail.

clue.text: In Florida tea consists of fruit

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words Florida tea

explanation.surface: In Florida, the tea is made from fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Declare that a fool never fasted

parts.note: an ass is a fool
if someone never fasted, they always ate: ever ate

explanation.surface: Someone states that an idiot has never gone without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to affirm solemnly.
